name: MULEGUARD core mule-account detection pack
description: Transparent, evidence-backed typology rules for suspected mule accounts. Investigative leads only; never proof of wrongdoing and never an automatic enforcement control.

calibration_notes: A single CRITICAL rule lands in the 'high' band, not 'critical': one typology alone should not top out the scale.
Two HIGH rules combine to ~0.84, which is the intended 'multiple independent typologies' signal.
Three MEDIUM rules combine to ~0.73, so corroborating weak evidence still surfaces an account.
LOW and INFO rules are context annotations; alone they cannot reach the review threshold.
interpretation_limits: Every rule describes observable transactional behaviour, not intent.
Shared devices, IPs, and UPI handles are associations only; families and shared devices are legitimate.
Complaint correlation indicates a reported incident, not an adjudicated outcome.
Rules must never be used to automatically freeze, block, or close an account.

rules.name: Rapid pass-through within 24 hours
rules.description: Funds arrive and leave almost immediately with little retained balance, the defining behaviour of a pass-through mule account.

conditions.description: At least six completed transfers in 24 hours.
At least 80% of monthly value moved outbound.
Inbound and outbound value nearly balance, so little is retained.
Mean gap between transfers under two hours.

action.reason_message: Inbound funds were forwarded almost immediately with minimal retained balance.

rules.name: Fan-in collection account
rules.description: Many distinct senders pay into one account over a short period, the classic victim-collection pattern.

conditions.description: Ten or more distinct paying counterparties.
Most counterparties are new to this account.
Inbound value is spread across many senders rather than one payroll source.

action.reason_message: Many unfamiliar senders paid into this account in a short window.

rules.name: Fan-out distribution account
rules.description: One account disperses funds to many beneficiaries, consistent with a distribution or smurfing leg.

conditions.description: Ten or more distinct receiving counterparties.
Predominantly outbound value.
Outbound value is dispersed rather than paid to one supplier.

action.reason_message: Funds were dispersed across many distinct beneficiaries.

rules.name: Layering intermediary position
rules.description: The account sits on many short paths between other accounts, acting as a hop in a layering chain rather than an endpoint.

conditions.description: High intermediary position score.
Sits on a large share of shortest paths.
Participates in at least five candidate fund-flow paths.

action.reason_message: The account acts as an intermediary hop across multiple fund-flow paths.

rules.name: Round-trip cycle participation
rules.description: Funds return to an earlier account in the chain, which has no ordinary commercial explanation at this scale.

conditions.description: Account participates in a detected transfer cycle.
Enough activity for the cycle to be meaningful.

action.reason_message: Funds circulated back to an earlier account in the chain.

rules.name: Dormant account reactivated at volume
rules.description: A long-dormant account suddenly transacts heavily, a common signature of a sold or taken-over account.

conditions.description: Account was dormant before the observation window.
At least five transfers in the last seven days.
At least a 200% increase against the prior week.

action.reason_message: A previously dormant account became highly active.

rules.name: New account with immediate high velocity
rules.description: A freshly opened account transacts at a rate unusual for a genuine new customer.

conditions.description: Account opened within the last 30 days.
At least five transfers in a single day.
Already transacting with several counterparties.

action.reason_message: A newly opened account immediately transacted at high velocity.

rules.name: Named as suspect in a recent cybercrime complaint
rules.description: A complainant named this account as the destination of defrauded funds. This is the strongest single corroborating signal available.

conditions.description: Named as a suspected account in at least one complaint.
The complaint was filed within the last 30 days.

action.reason_message: A recent cybercrime complaint named this account as a suspected recipient.

limits: A complaint is an allegation. It is not an adjudicated finding.

rules.name: Multiple independent complaints converge
rules.description: Several separate complaints reference this account, which is far less likely to be coincidence than a single report.

conditions.description: Three or more complaints reference this account.
A material share of activity is complaint-linked.

action.reason_message: Multiple independent complaints reference this account.

rules.name: Device shared across many accounts
rules.description: One device identifier is associated with an implausible number of accounts, suggesting centrally operated accounts.

conditions.description: Device linked to five or more accounts.
Most of those links are unverified.

action.reason_message: A single device is associated with an unusual number of accounts.

limits: Shared devices occur legitimately within families and small businesses.

rules.name: UPI handle shared across many accounts
rules.description: One UPI handle resolves to many accounts, a pattern seen in rented-account networks.

conditions.description: UPI handle linked to four or more accounts.

action.reason_message: A single UPI handle is associated with several accounts.

rules.name: Originating IP shared across many accounts
rules.description: Many accounts transact from one IP hash. Weaker than a device match because of carrier NAT and shared networks.

conditions.description: IP linked to eight or more accounts.

action.reason_message: Several accounts share an originating network address.

limits: Carrier NAT and public Wi-Fi make shared IPs common and weakly probative.

rules.name: Complaint-dense transaction neighbourhood
rules.description: Direct counterparties are themselves frequently complained about, indicating the account sits inside an implicated cluster.

conditions.description: A quarter or more of neighbours are complaint-linked.
Enough neighbours for the ratio to be meaningful.

action.reason_message: The account transacts with counterparties that are themselves complaint-linked.

rules.name: Uniform repeated amounts at volume
rules.description: Many transfers of near-identical value, consistent with structuring beneath a reporting or verification threshold.

conditions.description: At least eight transfers in a week.
Amounts vary by under 15%, so they are near-identical.

action.reason_message: Repeated transfers of near-identical value suggest structuring.

limits: Subscriptions, rent, and payroll also produce uniform amounts.

rules.name: Balance flushed to near zero
rules.description: The account is swept almost empty shortly after receiving funds, so value is not retained.

conditions.description: Balance fell by 85% or more within a week.
The drop was driven by transfers, not a single payment.

action.reason_message: The account balance was swept to near zero after funds arrived.

rules.name: Transfer amount far outside account norm
rules.description: A transfer sits many standard deviations above the account's own historical pattern.

conditions.description: At least three standard deviations above the account's own mean.
Enough history for a z-score to be meaningful.

action.reason_message: A transfer was far larger than this account's established pattern.

rules.name: Value funnelled to a single beneficiary
rules.description: Nearly all outbound value reaches one counterparty, the shape of a collection account forwarding to a controller.

conditions.description: One counterparty receives 80% or more of value.
Funds were collected from several senders first.
Predominantly outbound.

action.reason_message: Collected funds were forwarded almost entirely to one beneficiary.

rules.name: Activity concentrated in night hours
rules.description: Transfers cluster in night hours with little spread, a weak contextual signal on its own.

conditions.description: Most transfers occur during night hours.
Activity is concentrated in few hours of the day.
Enough transfers for the pattern to be real.

action.reason_message: Activity is concentrated in a narrow band of night hours.

limits: Shift workers and cross-timezone users transact at night legitimately.

rules.name: Frequent payment-channel switching
rules.description: Rapid alternation between payment rails, sometimes used to frustrate per-rail monitoring.

conditions.description: Six or more channel switches in a week.
Value genuinely spread across rails.

action.reason_message: The account alternates frequently between payment channels.

rules.name: Unsupervised velocity anomaly
rules.description: The unsupervised velocity detector places this account well outside the population norm.

conditions.description: High unsupervised velocity anomaly score.

action.reason_message: Transaction velocity is anomalous against the population baseline.

rules.name: Unsupervised network-position anomaly
rules.description: The account's graph position is unusual against the population of accounts of similar size.

conditions.description: High unsupervised network anomaly score.

action.reason_message: The account's network position is anomalous against the population baseline.

rules.name: Established merchant with stable counterparties
rules.description: Annotation only. A long-lived business account with high repeat custom and no complaints is the common false positive for fan-in rules; recording that context helps a triaging analyst dismiss quickly.

conditions.description: Registered as a business or merchant account.
Open for at least a year.
Most counterparties are returning.
No complaints reference this account.

action.reason_message: Long-established business account with stable repeat counterparties and no complaints.

limits: This is mitigating context for a human reader, not an exoneration.
It deliberately does not suppress other rules: a compromised merchant account must still surface.
